Name: Gaia BH1
Type: Dormant black hole binary (G dwarf companion)
Key Notes: Nearest known black hole; found from Gaia astrometry in 2022.

Name: Gaia BH3
Key Notes: Most massive known stellar black hole in the Milky Way (Gaia, 2024).

Name: A0620-00 (V616 Mon)
Key Notes: Nearest X-ray binary black hole; X-ray nova in 1975.

Name: Gaia BH2
Type: Dormant black hole binary (red giant companion)
Key Notes: Wide 1,277-day orbit around a red giant.

Name: XTE J1118+480 (KV UMa)
Key Notes: Lies far above the Galactic plane; outburst discovered in 2000.

Name: Cygnus X-1
Key Notes: First object widely accepted as a black hole; subject of the Hawking-Thorne bet.

Name: V404 Cygni
Key Notes: Distance from radio parallax; violent outbursts in 1989 and 2015.

Name: MAXI J1820+070 (ASASSN-18ey)
Key Notes: One of the brightest X-ray transients ever seen (2018); radio parallax distance.

Name: GRO J1655-40 (V1033 Sco)
Key Notes: Superluminal radio jets; distance debated (1.7-3.2 kpc).

Name: XTE J1550-564 (V381 Nor)
Key Notes: Large-scale X-ray jets seen decelerating over years.

Name: V4641 Sgr
Key Notes: Extremely rapid outburst in 1999; source of very-high-energy gamma rays.

Name: Sagittarius A*
Key Notes: Galactic Centre; mass from the orbit of star S2; imaged by the Event Horizon Telescope (2022).

Name: GRS 1915+105 (V1487 Aql)
Key Notes: First Galactic source with superluminal jets; radio parallax distance.
